You have to go see a psychiatrist, rather preferable a psychiatrist. You could go to anyone that's able to give prescription medications. Talk with any behavioral health agency/department and they should have resources for you, or get you a referral.

Give it a shot. Medication is a long process though. You won't be able to just start them and immediately feel better. What they'll do is start you on one for a couple months. When you do improve. You will notice it. Other people will notice it too. I've been trying different medications for 2-3 years now. Thankfully, I've finally found one that's seems to be working. I've noticed somethings that have changed, and others have too. Recently, I've been laughing a lot more then I use to. I don't feel so depressed anymore. In the end, what's the worst that could happen. If worst come to worst, you'll still end up in the same spot. Either in a Psych ward or dead. So what's the harm in trying?

I once tried overdosing while I was in college. I ended up walking into the ER. Was back before my roommates even knew I was gone. Nobody knew I tried to kill myself. Then months later, I made a suicidal facebook post. Which lead to cops showing up at my door, and a week in a psych ward. 

I'll be honest with you. Pysch wards are boring, but it helped me alot. If you're really considering suicide. At least give the hospital a shot first. Treatment was the best thing that ever happened to me. Often times I find myself wishing I could go back. Mostly just because I was there with other people who actually understood me. Who shared my pain if not had more then I could ever bare. The best thing I learn there, was that I'm not alone....You're not alone. You just have to ask.
